help.intro: A phone call of about one and a half minutes: a guest books a hotel room in Konstanz and has to spell her name, her e-mail address and her street. The receptionist uses the German spelling alphabet, the one every German knows from the phone: A wie Anton, B wie Berta, C wie Cäsar, and so on. The scene is invented; the spelling words are the real ones used in Germany. You hear what you have just learnt: the letters of the alphabet, numbers in a phone number, and the questions Wie heißen Sie? Wie schreibt man das? Wie ist Ihre Telefonnummer? Listen once for the whole call, then once more for each spelled word.
help.tips[0].title: The German spelling alphabet
help.tips[0].text: On the phone Germans say a letter and a name: A wie Anton, B wie Berta, C wie Cäsar, D wie Dora, E wie Emil, F wie Friedrich, G wie Gustav, H wie Heinrich, I wie Ida, J wie Julius, K wie Kaufmann, L wie Ludwig, M wie Martha, N wie Nordpol, O wie Otto, P wie Paula, Q wie Quelle, R wie Richard, S wie Samuel (or Siegfried), T wie Theodor, U wie Ulrich, V wie Viktor, W wie Wilhelm, X wie Xanthippe, Y wie Ypsilon, Z wie Zacharias. Umlauts: Ä wie Ärger, Ö wie Ökonom, Ü wie Übermut; ß = Eszett or scharfes S.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: My name is Kolb: K as in Kaufmann, O as in Otto, L as in Ludwig, B as in Berta.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: How do you write that, with V as in Viktor or with W as in Wilhelm?
help.tips[0].check.q: D wie Dora, O wie Otto, R wie Richard, N wie Nordpol spells:
help.tips[1].title: Letters that trip you up
help.tips[1].text: E is said eh, I is ih, A is ah: the opposite of English. V sounds like fau, W like veh. Y is Ypsilon, Z is tsett. J is yot. In e-mail addresses: @ = at (said the English way), . = Punkt, - = Bindestrich, _ = Unterstrich. Phone numbers are read in single digits or in pairs: null sieben fünf drei eins = 07531.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The address is lena dot kolb at mail dot de.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The area code is zero seven five three one.
help.tips[1].check.q: A German says the letter 'eh'. Which letter is it?
help.tips[1].check.why: German E = eh, German A = ah, German I = ih.
help.remember[0]: A wie Anton, B wie Berta, K wie Kaufmann, N wie Nordpol, V wie Viktor, W wie Wilhelm.
help.remember[1]: E = eh, I = ih, A = ah; @ = at, . = Punkt.
help.exam: Short phone calls in which a name or an address is spelled are a typical listening task at this level, and exactly what happens at every hotel desk and hotline.
help.hook: K wie Kaufmann, O wie Otto, L wie Ludwig, B wie Berta: listen to a hotel booking and write down the name, the e-mail and the street.
passageTranslation:
Reception: Hotel Seeblick Konstanz, good day, my name is Berger.
Guest: Good day. I would like to book a room, please. For two nights, Friday and Saturday.
Reception: Certainly. A single room or a double room?
Guest: A double room, please.
Reception: Good. What is your name, please?
Guest: Lena Kolb.
Reception: Kolb? How do you spell that?
Guest: K as in Kaufmann, O as in Otto, L as in Ludwig, B as in Berta. Kolb.
Reception: K, O, L, B. Thank you. And the first name is Lena, L, E, N, A?
Guest: Yes, exactly.
Reception: Do you have an e-mail address?
Guest: Yes. Lena dot Kolb at mail dot de. All lower case.
Reception: Lena dot Kolb at mail dot de. And your address?
Guest: Weberstraße 14, in Freiburg. Weber with W as in Wilhelm, E, B as in Berta, E, R. Straße with sharp S.
Reception: Weberstraße 14, Freiburg. And the postcode?
Guest: 79098. Seven, nine, zero, nine, eight.
Reception: Thank you. And a telephone number?
Guest: Zero one seven six, two four, eight eight, three one.
Reception: Zero one seven six, twenty-four, eighty-eight, thirty-one. Good. The double room costs ninety euros per night, with breakfast.
Guest: Ninety euros, good. Thank you very much!
Reception: Thank you, Ms Kolb. See you Friday!

questions[1].explanation: "K wie Kaufmann, O wie Otto, L wie Ludwig, B wie Berta. Kolb."
questions[1].questionTranslation: How do you spell the woman's family name?
questions[2].explanation: wie + a name is the German spelling alphabet: B wie Berta = the letter B, as in Berta.
questions[2].questionTranslation: 'B wie Berta': what does that mean?
questions[2].optionsTranslation[1]: The letter B, with the example word Berta
questions[3].explanation: "Lena Punkt Kolb at mail Punkt de." Punkt = dot.
questions[4].explanation: "Weberstraße 14, in Freiburg." Konstanz is where the hotel is.
questions[6].explanation: "Null eins sieben sechs, zwei vier, acht acht, drei eins." The receptionist repeats it in pairs: vierundzwanzig, achtundachtzig, einunddreißig.
questions[7].explanation: "Das Doppelzimmer kostet neunzig Euro pro Nacht, mit Frühstück."
questions[7].questionTranslation: What does the room cost per night?
